sections.html:
Cobb's county and school levies are combined on one statement mailed by the Tax Commissioner, who collects on behalf of the commissioners and the school board. If your lot lies outside every city, that is the only bill. A parcel in Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna or Powder Springs gets a second bill, because each of those seven cities collects for itself.

Valuation is someone else's job. The Board of Tax Assessors determines fair market value annually, and 40% of that figure is what gets taxed. The formula reads (Fair Market Value x 0.40) x (Millage Rate / 1,000), and one mill is $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. Rates are chosen yearly by the county, the schools and each city on its own.

When the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant applies to an eligible homestead, you will see it as its own reduction line, apart from any exemption.

Mailing happens by August 15 and the deadline is October 15. The tax digest has to be approved first, usually in mid to late July, and until then the office cannot take money, so prepaying is impossible.

Payment counts as timely when the office holds it by October 15 or when a Postal Service postmark shows that date at the latest. Meter and kiosk stamps are rejected. No bill by August 30? Print a copy from the commissioner's website, because a lost bill is no defense against penalty or interest.

Partial payments are welcome, yet any balance left after October 15 picks up a 5% penalty along with monthly interest. Call 770-528-8600 to work out an arrangement. Bounced checks cost $30 or 5%, whichever is larger, plus bank charges.

Pick from four methods:

  • Online by e-check or card, with no convenience fee on e-check
  • Phone, at 1-866-535-2622
  • Mail, to P.O. Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061
  • In person or by drop box at the offices below

The county keeps none of the card fees.

With an escrow account, once the lender notifies the office, bills are sent to you and the lender alike. Verifying that the payment went through is still on you. A double payment is refunded. The payment coupon is optional as long as the parcel ID is written on the check.

sections.h2: If you disagree with your valuation
sections.html:
Put your dispute in writing and deliver it to the Board of Tax Assessors inside 45 days of the notice date. The commissioner plays no role. You can contest value, uniformity or taxability, but the millage rate is off limits. When the assessors do not settle it, the case goes to the Board of Equalization.

Appealing leaves the deadline where it is. A parcel in dispute is billed a reduced appeal amount, either 85% of assessed value or 100% of the last uncontested value. Pay at least that by October 15 and the 5% penalty is avoided. The unpaid remainder can gather up to $150 a month in interest, which full payment on time prevents.

The commissioner's online estimator uses the prior year's millage rates and figures county tax only, leaving out city tax and special classifications. A second version for new home buyers takes a market value, a tax district and exemptions. Whatever either shows, the official bill controls.

Owners who occupy the house as their main home on January 1 qualify for the basic homestead exemption. At 62, seniors can claim additional breaks, among them a full or reduced school tax exemption. More exemptions exist for owners with a 100% service-connected disability, other disabled owners, surviving spouses of certain public servants, nonprofits and religious groups.

Applications can go in online, at an office or by mail, and they need to arrive or be postmarked ahead of the appeal deadline printed on your assessment notice. Later ones roll to next year. Held an exemption elsewhere before? Add a letter proving it was removed. Rentals cannot carry a homestead, and keeping one after you stop qualifying means paying back the savings with penalties and interest.

After a marriage, divorce, death or change in ownership, file a new application with the supporting paper: a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Special classifications such as conservation use, historic property and forest land go through the assessors.

sections.h2: When Cobb County taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
A late account first draws a written notice. After another 30 days the office may issue a Fi. Fa., a tax execution that acts as a lien. It adds $23 when the tax is under $100 or $33 when it is over $100, along with administrative costs, and late fees are not waived.

When a sale is scheduled, it happens on the first Tuesday of the month at Superior Court Plaza, corner of Haynes Street and Washington Avenue. You must pre-register and bid in person between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Winners pay in cash or by certified check. The thing sold is a tax deed, not a lien. The former owner then has 12 months to redeem by paying the bid, later taxes the buyer covered, special assessments, and a premium of 20% for the first year or fraction and 10% for each year after.

  • Request a written payoff before the house is listed.
  • If a Fi. Fa. has been filed, its fee is part of the payoff.
  • Once a tax sale occurs, the 12-month redemption window starts.

Prorating is not part of the commissioner's work. The parcel carries one full year of tax, and the closing paperwork decides who pays what when the sale closes. Because the tax stays with the property, whoever holds title at the time should see that it gets paid.

Once the sale closes, tell the commissioner about the new owner and have your homestead exemption taken off. The buyer applies for theirs as described above. Before listing or signing a contract, collect:

  • Your current bill and your most recent assessment notice
  • Any city bill for the same parcel
  • Notes on any appeal still open

Tenants, repairs or a delinquent bill do not stop a sale, and any payoff is taken from your proceeds in every case. A cash buyer is not waiting on a lender, so a clear payoff figure keeps a quick closing on schedule.

faqs.q: When do Cobb County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: The deadline is October 15, and bills are mailed by August 15. A payment is timely if it reaches the office or carries a Postal Service postmark by then. Anything unpaid afterward draws a 5% penalty and monthly interest.

faqs.q: Does Cobb County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Not formally. The office takes partial payments, but the balance left after October 15 keeps accruing penalty and interest. Call 770-528-8600 to arrange something. An appeal does not defer payment, though only the appeal amount is due by the deadline.

faqs.q: Will Cobb County split the tax bill between me and the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The bill covers the entire year, and the office leaves the split to you and the buyer. Your closing paperwork sets each side's share, and the closing attorney or title company normally pays out of proceeds.

faqs.q: What if my Cobb County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: You still owe it, penalty and interest included. Print a copy from the commissioner's website and write the parcel ID on your check, or call 770-528-8600. Fix your mailing address so it does not happen again.

faqs.q: How long can an owner redeem after a Cobb County tax sale?
faqs.a: For 12 months after the sale. The owner, a creditor or any other interested party can redeem by paying the bid, later taxes, special assessments and the stepped premium of 20% then 10%. The buyer works out the exact figure.
